stem.id: The report, together with its three appendices, ___ due on Friday.
stem.en: The report, together with its three appendices, ___ due on Friday.

explanation.pola: The subject is “the report” (singular); “together with …” does not change the number.
explanation.langkah: Strip the interrupting phrase: “The report ___ due on Friday.”
explanation.cepat: Find the head noun before any comma phrase.

stem.id: By the time the auditors arrive, we ___ the reconciliation.
stem.en: By the time the auditors arrive, we ___ the reconciliation.

explanation.pola: A future action completed before another future point takes the future perfect.
explanation.langkah: “By the time X happens” (future) → “will have + past participle”.
explanation.jebakan: “Had finished” is the past perfect, for a past reference point.
explanation.cepat: “By the time” + future event → will have.

stem.id: Neither the supervisor nor the technicians ___ aware of the new procedure.
stem.en: Neither the supervisor nor the technicians ___ aware of the new procedure.

explanation.pola: With “neither … nor”, the verb agrees with the nearer subject (“technicians”, plural).
explanation.jebakan: Choosing the singular because “neither” sounds singular.
explanation.cepat: Neither/nor: look right, agree with the closest.

stem.id: If the shipment ___ on time, the plant would not have stopped for two days.
stem.en: If the shipment ___ on time, the plant would not have stopped for two days.

explanation.pola: Third conditional: “if + past perfect, would have + past participle”.
explanation.langkah: Main clause “would not have stopped” signals an unreal past → if-clause past perfect.
explanation.jebakan: Mixing second conditional (“arrived”) with a third-conditional main clause.
explanation.cepat: “would have” in the main clause → “had” in the if-clause.

stem.id: Our team has worked on this project ___ March.
stem.en: Our team has worked on this project ___ March.

explanation.pola: “Since” marks the starting point of a period with the present perfect; “for” marks the length.
explanation.langkah: “March” is a point in time → since.
explanation.jebakan: “For March” would wrongly suggest a duration.
explanation.cepat: Point in time → since; length of time → for.

stem.id: The new policy, ___ was announced last week, applies to all branches.
stem.en: The new policy, ___ was announced last week, applies to all branches.

explanation.pola: A non-defining relative clause (between commas) uses “which”, never “that”.
explanation.langkah: Commas around the clause → non-defining → which.
explanation.jebakan: “That” is only for defining clauses without commas.

stem.en: Hardly ___ the meeting when the fire alarm went off.

explanation.pola: After a negative adverb at the front (“hardly”), subject and auxiliary invert; “hardly … when” takes the past perfect.
explanation.langkah: Hardly + had + subject + past participle + when.
